filename: Benchmarking of machine learning ocean subgrid parameterizations in an idealized model.pdf
title: Benchmarking of machine learning ocean subgrid parameterizations in an idealized model
venue: Earth and Space Science Open Archive (ESSOAr)
parameterization_target: Ocean mesoscale eddy subgrid forcing (potential vorticity tendency, momentum tendency, and subgrid fluxes)
testbed_rationale: Introduces an open-source benchmark framework with published datasets and code specifically designed for training and evaluating data-driven ocean subgrid parameterizations both offline and online across multiple flow regimes.
pain_points: Offline skill (high R^2) does not necessarily correspond to good online physical fidelity or stability.
Choice of coarse-graining and filtering operator drastically impacts online performance.
Neural network parameterizations generalize poorly across different dynamical flow regimes (e.g. transferring from eddy configuration to jet configuration).
Parameterizations improve long-term statistical metrics but can degrade short-term trajectory skill (decorrelation times).
Standard sparse symbolic regression scales poorly with higher-order spatial derivatives.
extraction_notes: The preprint was submitted to JAMES; dataset and benchmark repository versions are openly available on Zenodo.
